ai.title: Apply file changes with directory creation
ai.summary: Added recursive directory creation before file writes in `applyChanges` within `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`. Prevents errors when applying patches to files in non-existent directories.

eli5.text: When the assistant applies a batch of file edits, it now automatically creates any missing folders needed before writing the files. Previously, trying to write a file into a folder that didn't exist would fail with an error, leaving the edit incomplete. Now those folders are created on the fly, so edits to files in new or deeply nested locations apply correctly.

ai.title: Implement 100k token budget for file context
ai.summary: Added `getTruncatedFilesBasedOnTokenBudget` in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to limit file context to 100,000 tokens using new `tiktoken` dependency. Files exceeding the budget are replaced with `[TRUNCATED TO FIT TOKEN BUDGET]` marker. Includes new `backend/src/util/token-counter.ts` for token counting logic and moves `debug.ts` to `backend/src/util/debug.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to work on your project, it reads through your files to understand the context. This change puts a cap on how much of those files it reads at once, keeping the most important files first until it hits a limit of 100,000 tokens of text. Any file that would push it over that limit gets shortened and marked as truncated, so the system doesn't get overwhelmed by very large files or projects with tons of content. This affects anyone using the assistant to review big codebases, and you'd notice it if you're working on a project where some of your files suddenly show up with a truncation notice instead of full content.

ai.title: Split todo.knowledge.md from musings.knowledge.md
ai.summary: New todo.knowledge.md file created to hold task lists and problem tracking, extracted from musings.knowledge.md. Musings.knowledge.md retains high-level ideas and wish lists. This separates actionable items from conceptual notes.

eli5.text: The project's notes were mixed together in one place, so the team split them into two: one for big-picture wishes and one for specific tasks that need getting done. This mainly affects the developers working on the project, who now have a cleaner, action-focused list to track and check off problems. If you looked at the notes now, you would see the to-do items like fixing bugs with pasting text and handling file changes organized separately from the brainstorming ideas about new features.

ai.title: CLI paste detection via input timing
ai.summary: Added `detectPasting` and `isPasting` to `CLI` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to suppress `handleUserInput` during rapid input bursts. Mechanism tracks `lastInputTime` and `consecutiveFastInputs` on `line` and `keypress` events, treating inputs <5ms apart as paste. Scope limited to CLI core; `todo.knowledge.md` marks the feature complete. Threshold requires 2+ fast inputs to trigger paste state.

eli5.text: When you paste a large block of text into the assistant all at once, the typing can happen so fast that each keystroke arrives within a few milliseconds of the previous one. The system now watches how quickly consecutive inputs arrive and, once it sees that burst speed, it silently skips running your commands line by line during that flood instead of trying to process them mid-paste. You would mainly notice this if you pasted a big chunk of text and the assistant did not react to every line as it arrived. This is a small behind-the-scenes improvement and only affects the part of the tool that reads your keyboard input.

ai.title: CLI paste detection buffers newlines
ai.summary: Refactor CLI input handling in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to buffer pasted content across newlines. Replaced immediate line processing with `handleInput` that accumulates lines when `isPasting` is true. Prevents multi-line pastes from triggering separate responses.

eli5.text: When you paste several lines into the assistant at once, it now waits to receive the entire block before responding, instead of answering line by line. The assistant notices when you type or paste quickly and, after detecting that pattern, collects the remaining lines as part of a single message. If you paste a multi-line question or code snippet, you will see one coherent response rather than several separate ones triggered by each line.

ai.title: manicode 1.0.36
ai.summary: Version bump in npm-app/package.json. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number was bumped up by one, changing it from 1.0.35 to 1.0.36, though nothing about how it works actually changed. This is purely an internal label update that has no effect on features or performance, and if you looked at the project files you would only see that single number updated. It is live today but does nothing new.

ai.title: System prompt tweaks
ai.summary: System prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` reorders brainstorming steps and adds explicit instruction to minimize edits. Uncertainty scoring moved before plan selection, and a new `<important_instruction>` block mandates preserving existing behavior. Unused `countTokens` import removed.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to plan something, it now lists all possible plans first, then rates how uncertain it is about what you want. Before this tweak, assistants could over-edit or rewrite code unnecessarily, so the change nudges the logic to make smaller, more careful changes and stick to what you actually asked for. If you use the assistant today, you'll notice its reasoning flow feels more deliberate, and you should see fewer unexpected edits to your existing code.
